lean.fidelity_note: Let $0<T\le1$ and let $U$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent, with flow $X$, $F=D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Under $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$, the formal theorem has the endpoint conclusion of Theorem 4.2 for every $L\in C([0,T];C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3))$. It gives divergence-free $z\in C^1([0,T];C^{0,1/2})$ and $v=z_t$, a time-independent divergence-free $c$, and a continuous Hölder pressure gradient satisfying $Kv-\int_0^t\Omega v+L=c+\nabla_a\phi$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$. Uniqueness is of $z,v,c,\nabla_a\phi$, with equality of time-dependent fields on $[0,T]$; the scalar potential retains its arbitrary function of time. The bound is $C(D_-+L_M+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1)^p$, where these numbers bound $F^{-1}$, $M$, the coefficients and their first label derivatives in supremum norm, and $C\ge0$ and the nonnegative integer $p$ are chosen before all parent data. Here $L_M$ denotes the bound for $M$, to distinguish it from the source $L$. This is quantitatively stronger than (4.10), which uses full $C^{1,1/2}$ coefficient norms; those norms control the displayed bounds up to an absolute constant. A separate supplied inverse estimate uses exponent $4\cdot291=1164$; the formal statement of Theorem 4.2 leaves $p$ existential. The $C^{0,1/2}$ norm is the maximum of supremum norm and half-Hölder seminorm. For $L=-\int_0^tF^T(f\circ X)$ with smooth periodic $f$, the formal statement also gives smooth $z$, a smooth zero-spatial-mean label pressure satisfying (4.11), smooth $b=(Fv)\circ X^{-1}$ and $q$ solving (4.12), and $b(0)=c$. The same bound controls the fixed-time inverse on divergence-free Hölder fields. No Euler equation for the parent is assumed.
